findings.title: No post-quantum key exchange
findings.detail: The server accepts no hybrid ML-KEM group. Key exchange is classical only (ECDHE or RSA), which a quantum computer will be able to break with Shor's algorithm: traffic captured today could be decrypted in the future ("harvest now, decrypt later"). This is the most urgent quantum risk because it affects data already in transit.
findings.remediation: Enable the hybrid group X25519MLKEM768 in TLS 1.3: OpenSSL 3.5+, BoringSSL, Go 1.24+, Caddy 2.10+, nginx built with OpenSSL 3.5, or your CDN or load balancer's post-quantum option. Keep X25519 as a fallback for older clients.

findings.title: Without TLS 1.3, hybrid ML-KEM key exchange cannot be adopted
findings.detail: The server only accepts versions older than TLS 1.3. That may be secure today, but hybrid ML-KEM groups only exist in TLS 1.3: until it is enabled, traffic stays exposed to "harvest now, decrypt later" and no group configuration can fix it.
findings.remediation: Enable TLS 1.3 (any server with OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later supports it, as do all current browsers), then the X25519MLKEM768 group. Keep TLS 1.2 for older clients.

findings.title: 3DES cipher accepted
findings.detail: 3DES uses 64-bit blocks and is vulnerable to Sweet32 on long connections. Suites: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.
findings.remediation: Remove the 3DES suites and use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

findings.title: RC4 cipher accepted
findings.detail: RC4 has exploitable statistical biases and is prohibited in TLS (RFC 7465). Suites: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA.

findings.title: Classical signature (RSA-2048): future quantum risk
findings.detail: The server proves its identity with RSA-2048, which a quantum computer will be able to forge. This is not "harvest now, decrypt later": a signature only has to hold during the handshake, so the risk starts the day such a computer exists, not before. There are no post-quantum (ML-DSA) certificates on the public web yet. It does not affect the grade.
findings.remediation: Nothing to do on the signature yet. Automate renewal (ACME) so you can switch to post-quantum (ML-DSA or hybrid) certificates as soon as authorities issue them: today this certificate shows no sign of renewing itself.

findings.title: No sign of automated renewal
findings.detail: 90-day validity, issued by QuantumReady TLS lab. Maximum certificate validity is already 200 days (since 15 March 2026) and will drop to 100 days on 15 March 2027 and to 47 on 15 March 2029 (CA/Browser Forum ballot SC-081). Moving to post-quantum certificates will require reissuing them: without automation, every change is manual work and an expiry risk.
findings.remediation: Automate issuance and renewal with ACME (certbot, Caddy, cert-manager…), with your current authority if it supports it or a free one.

findings.title: Weak elliptic curves accepted: secp224r1
findings.detail: The server accepts curves under 256 bits or deprecated ones (RFC 8422, RFC 9847). Browsers never offer them, so they only affect old or misconfigured clients; that is why they do not cap the grade.
findings.remediation: Keep only x25519, secp256r1 and secp384r1 (and the hybrid ML-KEM groups).

findings.title: CBC-mode suites
findings.detail: TLS 1.2 CBC mode has suffered padding-oracle attacks (Lucky13 and the like) and depends on careful implementations. Suites: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384.
findings.remediation: Prefer AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and remove CBC ones if your clients allow it.

findings.title: No transparency SCTs
findings.detail: No SCTs were found (neither embedded nor in the handshake). Browsers require them for public certificates, so this usually means a private certificate. Informational.

findings.title: Valid certificate
findings.detail: The chain is trusted, matches the name and is current (issuer: QuantumReady TLS lab; expires in 46 days).

findings.title: Forward secrecy
findings.detail: Every connection uses an ephemeral key exchange: even if the server's private key leaked, it would not decrypt past connections.

not_evaluated.label: PSK, SRP, Kerberos and GOST suites (they need credentials or algorithms a scanner does not have)
